marble.name: Subject-verb agreement
marble.subject: English
marble.description: Use singular and plural nouns with matching verbs in sentences, maintaining subject-verb agreement (e.g., 'He hops' vs 'We hop')
marble.prompt: If you writes "she hop" or "we hops", do they catch the mistake — and can they fix it to "she hops" and "we hop" so the subject and verb match?

cluster.summary: Your child is learning the building blocks of writing — how to make complete sentences, use capital letters and punctuation marks correctly, and understand basic word types like nouns and verbs.

representations: Subject-verb matching cards (the dog runs / the dogs run)
Singular/plural subject sort including irregular plurals
Who-or-what arrow from verb to subject
authoredAnswer: "The baby sleeps in the pram." "My brothers like pizza." "The mice run under the bed." "She fixes the bike." is already correct. "We hop over the puddles." The check finds the subject (baby, brothers, mice, she, we), decides one or more than one, and chooses -s for singular subjects other than I/you and the base form for plurals.

wrongAnswers.revealedBy: Treats irregular plurals (mice, children, people) as singular because they lack -s. Evidence basis: Common Core State Standards for English Language Arts, Language standards, Grade 1. This is an authored observable perfo
wrongAnswers.fix: Pair mouse/mice and child/children with counters; read "one mouse runs, three mice run" and add irregular plural subjects to the sort.

wrongAnswers.revealedBy: Drops the -s or -es on verbs after singular subjects, or changes a correct sentence. Evidence basis: Common Core State Standards for English Language Arts, Language standards, Grade 1. This is an authored observable perf
wrongAnswers.fix: Say pairs aloud (I fix / she fixes) and highlight the -es; check whether the original sentence needed changing before editing.
